title: Generate datapoints — rPr
code: ## Use the "K" object 'Kexample' included in *Prova*, ## calculated from the "penguins" dataset. ## Variates: 'species' and 'bill_len'  ## ## Example 1: ## Generate 10 values of the 'species' variate, ## with the same probability calculated from the data datapoints <- rPr(n = 10, Ynames = 'species', K = Kexample) ## alternatively: rPr(10, 'species', NA, Kexample) datapoints #>      species #> 1     Adelie #> 2     Gentoo #> 3     Adelie #> 4     Gentoo #> 5  Chinstrap #> 6     Adelie #> 7  Chinstrap #> 8     Adelie #> 9     Gentoo #> 10    Adelie   ## ## Example 2: ## Generate 5 joint values of 'species' and 'bill_len' variates. datapoints <- rPr(5, c('species', 'bill_len'), NA, Kexample) datapoints #>     species bill_len #> 1    Adelie     38.3 #> 2    Gentoo     46.0 #> 3    Adelie     41.5 #> 4 Chinstrap     54.7 #> 5    Adelie     42.0   ## ## Example 3: ## Generate 5 values of the 'species' variate, ## among penguins having bill length shorter than or equal to 40 mm  datapoints <- rPr(5, 'species', data.frame(bill_len = 40), Kexample, tails = list(bill_len = '<=')) datapoints #>   species #> 1  Adelie #> 2  Adelie #> 3  Adelie #> 4  Adelie #> 5  Adelie   ## ## Example 4: ## To omit 'K =' arguments, set a default one with useK() useK(Kexample)  ## Generate 10 values of the 'species' variate. ## The datapoints are different from before, ## since we did not set a random seed with 'set.seed()' datapoints <- rPr(10, 'species') datapoints #>      species #> 1     Gentoo #> 2     Gentoo #> 3     Gentoo #> 4     Adelie #> 5     Adelie #> 6     Adelie #> 7     Gentoo #> 8     Adelie #> 9  Chinstrap #> 10    Gentoo  ## Remove any default 'K =' argument useK(NA)

code: ## Load the example `K`nowledge object calculated from the "penguins" dataset; ## variates: 'species' and 'bill_len' K <- Kexample  ## Calculate the probability object for the three values of variate 'species', ## given values 43 to 45 of variate 'bill_len'; ## this object contains probabilities, quantiles, and other information probs <- Pr(   Y = data.frame(species = c('Adelie', 'Chinstrap', 'Gentoo')),   X = data.frame(bill_len = c(43, 45)),   K = K )  probs$value #>            |bill_len #> species            43         45 #>   Adelie    0.4581298 0.08803413 #>   Chinstrap 0.1517864 0.25467171 #>   Gentoo    0.3900838 0.65729416  ## Subset by retaining the values 'Adelie' and 'Gentoo' for species, ## and 44 or less for bill length newprobs <- subset(   probs,   subsetY = (species %in% c('Adelie', 'Gentoo')),   subsetX = (bill_len <= 44) )  newprobs$value #>         |bill_len #> species         43 #>   Adelie 0.4581298 #>   Gentoo 0.3900838  ## Plot these conditional probabilities and their revisabilities plot(newprobs)   hist(newprobs)

code: ## Use the "K" object 'Kexample', ## calculated from the "penguins" dataset; ## variates: 'species' and 'bill_len'  ## set of values for the variate "species"; ## since this variate is of a nominal kind, all values are included valuesSpecies <- vrtgrid('species', Kexample)  print(valuesSpecies) #>     species #> 1    Adelie #> 2 Chinstrap #> 3    Gentoo  ## create a small set of values for the variate "bill length"; ## this variate is continuous and rounded valuesBill <- vrtgrid('bill_len', Kexample, length.out = 4)  print(valuesBill) #>   bill_len #> 1 27.50000 #> 2 39.73333 #> 3 51.96667 #> 4 64.20000  ## calculate the conditional probabilities for the 'bill_len' values above, ## given the values of 'species' probs <- Pr(valuesBill, valuesSpecies, Kexample)   ## Create a data frame with all possible combinations of the values above;
